Addition and subtraction of ordered pairs are componentwise:

q: Find the product \( (2,\, -1)(3,\, 2) \) in the form \( (x,\, y) \).
c:
Solution

The product of ordered pairs is

\((x_1,y_1)(x_2,y_2)=(x_1 x_2-y_1 y_2,\; x_1 y_2+y_1 x_2).\)


Hence

\[\begin{aligned}(2,-1)(3,2)&= \bigl(2\cdot 3-(-1)\cdot 2,\; 2\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 3\bigr)\\&= (6+2,\; 4-3)\\&= (8,\; 1).\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \((8,\, 1)\)

q: Find the multiplicative inverse \( z^{-1} \) of \( z=2+i \).
c:
Solution

We have \( z^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{2+i} \). Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \( 2-i \):

\[\begin{aligned}z^{-1}&= \frac{2-i}{(2+i)(2-i)}= \frac{2-i}{4+1}= \frac{2-i}{5}\\&= \frac{2}{5}-\frac{1}{5}i.\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \(\dfrac{2}{5}-\dfrac{1}{5}i\)

Solution

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \( 2+i \):

\[\begin{aligned}\frac{1+3i}{2-i}&= \frac{(1+3i)(2+i)}{(2-i)(2+i)}= \frac{2+i+6i+3i^2}{4+1}\\&= \frac{2+7i-3}{5}= \frac{-1+7i}{5}\\&= -\frac{1}{5}+\frac{7}{5}i.\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \(-\dfrac{1}{5}+\dfrac{7}{5}i\)

q: Express \( z=-\sqrt{3}-i \) in trigonometric form with \( -\pi<\theta\le\pi \).
c:
Solution

The modulus is

\(r=\sqrt{(-\sqrt{3})^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{3+1}=2.\)


Then \( \cos\theta=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \) and \( \sin\theta=-\dfrac{1}{2} \), so \( \theta \) lies in the third quadrant. The principal value is \( \theta=-\dfrac{5\pi}{6} \).

Hence

\(z=2\Bigl(\cos\Bigl(-\frac{5\pi}{6}\Bigr)+i\sin\Bigl(-\frac{5\pi}{6}\Bigr)\Bigr).\)


Answer   \(2\Bigl(\cos\Bigl(-\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\Bigr)+i\sin\Bigl(-\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\Bigr)\Bigr)\)

q: Express \( z=1+\sqrt{3}\, i \) in trigonometric form with \( -\pi<\theta\le\pi \).
c:
Solution

The modulus is

\(r=\sqrt{1^2+(\sqrt{3})^2}=\sqrt{1+3}=2.\)


Then \( \cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2} \) and \( \sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \), so \( \theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3} \).

Hence

\(z=2\Bigl(\cos\frac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\Bigr).\)


Answer   \(2\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\bigr)\)

q: Find the product of \( z_1=4\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\bigr) \) and \( z_2=\dfrac12\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{12}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}\bigr) \) in trigonometric form.
c:
Solution

If \( z_1=r_1(\cos\theta_1+i\sin\theta_1) \) and \( z_2=r_2(\cos\theta_2+i\sin\theta_2) \), then

\(z_1 z_2=r_1 r_2\bigl(\cos(\theta_1+\theta_2)+i\sin(\theta_1+\theta_2)\bigr).\)


So

\[\begin{aligned}z_1 z_2&= 4\cdot\frac12\Bigl(\cos\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{12}\Bigr)+i\sin\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{12}\Bigr)\Bigr)\\&= 2\Bigl(\cos\frac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\Bigr).\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \(2\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\bigr)\)

Solution

Division of trigonometric forms is given by

\(\frac{z_1}{z_2}=\frac{r_1}{r_2}\bigl(\cos(\theta_1-\theta_2)+i\sin(\theta_1-\theta_2)\bigr).\)


Hence

\[\begin{aligned}\frac{z_1}{z_2}&= \frac{6}{3}\Bigl(\cos\Bigl(\frac{5\pi}{6}-\frac{\pi}{2}\Bigr)+i\sin\Bigl(\frac{5\pi}{6}-\frac{\pi}{2}\Bigr)\Bigr)\\&= 2\Bigl(\cos\frac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\Bigr).\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \(2\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\bigr)\)

Solution

The powers of \( i \) repeat every four: \( i^1=i,\; i^2=-1,\; i^3=-i,\; i^4=1 \).

\[\begin{aligned}i^{41}&= (i^4)^{10}\cdot i=i,\\i^{42}&= (i^4)^{10}\cdot i^2=-1.\end{aligned}\]


Therefore

\(i^{41}+i^{42}=i+(-1)=-1+i.\)


Answer   \(-1+i\)

q: If \( z=2\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\bigr) \), find \( z^3 \) in trigonometric form.
c:
Solution

By De Moivre's theorem, \( \bigl[r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)\bigr]^n=r^n\bigl(\cos n\theta+i\sin n\theta\bigr) \).

\[\begin{aligned}z^3&= 2^3\Bigl(\cos\Bigl(3\cdot\frac{\pi}{6}\Bigr)+i\sin\Bigl(3\cdot\frac{\pi}{6}\Bigr)\Bigr)\\&= 8\Bigl(\cos\frac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{2}\Bigr).\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \(8\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\bigr)\)

q: Find the square roots of \( z=9\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\bigr) \) in trigonometric form.
c:
Solution

The \( n \)-th roots of \( r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta) \) are

\(w_k=\sqrt[n]{r}\left(\cos\frac{\theta+2k\pi}{n}+i\sin\frac{\theta+2k\pi}{n}\right),\quad k=0,1,\ldots,n-1.\)


Here \( n=2 \), \( r=9 \), \( \theta=\dfrac{\pi}{2} \).

\[\begin{aligned}k=0:\quad w_0&=3\Bigl(\cos\frac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\Bigr),\\k=1:\quad w_1&=3\Bigl(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4}+i\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\Bigr).\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \( 3\bigl(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\bigr) \) and \( 3\bigl(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{4}\bigr) \)

q: Find the real and imaginary parts of \( \dfrac{4+3i}{2+i} \).
c:
Solution

Multiply numerator and denominator by \( 2-i \):

\[\begin{aligned}\frac{4+3i}{2+i}&= \frac{(4+3i)(2-i)}{(2+i)(2-i)}= \frac{8-4i+6i-3i^2}{4+1}\\&= \frac{8+2i+3}{5}= \frac{11+2i}{5}\\&= \frac{11}{5}+\frac{2}{5}i.\end{aligned}\]


So the real part is \( \dfrac{11}{5} \) and the imaginary part is \( \dfrac{2}{5} \).

Answer   real \( \dfrac{11}{5} \), imaginary \( \dfrac{2}{5} \)

q: Find the distance between the points representing \( z_1=2+5i \) and \( z_2=-1+i \) in the complex plane.

c:
Solution

First expand \( z \):

\[\begin{aligned}z&=(3-i)(2+2i)=6+6i-2i-2i^2\\&=6+4i+2=8+4i.\end{aligned}\]


Changing the sign of the imaginary part gives \( \bar{z}=8-4i \).

Answer   \(8-4i\)
